chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the man whose back is broken, he said: For it is the complete wergild; and for the two eyes is the (complete) wergild, and for one of them is half the wergild; and for the two ears is the (complete) wergild, and for one of them is half the wergild; and for the penis, when the foreskin and what is above it is cut off, is the (complete) wergild; and for the nose, when the soft part is cut off, is the wergild; and for the two lips is the (complete) wergild.
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money compensation for breaking the back or injuring the eyes and ears according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides a detailed jurisprudential breakdown of *diyah* (blood money) for specific bodily injuries, establishing the legal precedents for full, half, or proportional compensation based on the severity and location of the wound. It reflects the Imami Shia tradition's precise categorization of *khasa'is* (distinctive injuries), linking physical integrity to financial restitution as a means of justice and deterrence. The text serves as a foundational source for *fiqh al-jaraha* (injury jurisprudence), illustrating how minor wounds are quantified relative to the complete wergild paid for a life.
